english.title: Foreigner fail to notify change of address within 8 days
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an alien who had furnished particulars under regulation 5 of the Immigration (Registration with Police) Regulations 1972 and not having a residence in the United Kingdom, failed, without reasonable excuse, on moving from one address to another to notify the appropriate registration officer of your arrival there within 8 days of your arrival.
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 7(4) of the Immigration (Registration with Police) Regulations 1972 and section 26(1)(f) of the Immigration Act 1971.

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 7(4) does not apply unless the alien remains or intends to remain at the address beyond 7 days (regulation 7(5)).
(ii) The term 'alien' is used in the actual legislation and it would therefore be inappropriate to change the wording. However, in day to day speech the term 'foreign national' is more acceptable.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
